questions.question: What is the primary diagnostic IR absorption band for the characteristic functional group of Chapter 12?

options.label: A
options.text: Characteristic diagnostic vibrational absorption corresponding to the core Chapter 12 functional group stretching mode.

options.label: B
options.text: A single broad peak at 4000 cm⁻¹.

options.label: C
options.text: Absence of any vibrational modes.

options.label: D
options.text: Weak background noise below 500 cm⁻¹.

questions.correct_answer: Characteristic diagnostic vibrational absorption corresponding to the core Chapter 12 functional group stretching mode.
questions.explanation: Every functional group in Chapter 12 displays a characteristic diagnostic infrared absorption frequency.

questions.question: Applying the (n+1) splitting rule, what multiplicity is predicted for a proton with n equivalent neighboring protons in Chapter 12?

options.label: A
options.text: A singlet with n peaks.

options.label: B
options.text: A doublet with 2n peaks.

options.label: C
options.text: A multiplet with (n + 1) distinct peaks with intensity ratios determined by Pascal's triangle in Chapter 12.

options.label: D
options.text: Zero splitting regardless of neighbors.

questions.correct_answer: A multiplet with (n + 1) distinct peaks with intensity ratios determined by Pascal's triangle in Chapter 12.
questions.explanation: Scalar spin-spin coupling splits NMR signals into (n+1) peaks where n is the number of vicinal equivalent protons.

questions.question: How many distinct ¹³C NMR signals are observed for a symmetric molecule in Chapter 12?

options.label: A
options.text: Always exactly equal to the total number of carbons regardless of symmetry.

options.label: B
options.text: The number of signals equals the number of chemically and magnetically non-equivalent carbon sets in the Chapter 12 structure.

options.label: C
options.text: Zero signals in decoupled mode.

options.label: D
options.text: Always exactly one signal.

questions.correct_answer: The number of signals equals the number of chemically and magnetically non-equivalent carbon sets in the Chapter 12 structure.
questions.explanation: Molecular symmetry reduces the number of unique carbon resonance peaks in broadband proton-decoupled 13C NMR.

questions.question: In Chapter 12 spectral analysis, how does DEPT-135 identify a quaternary carbon?

options.label: A
options.text: Quaternary carbons appear at δ 0 ppm.

options.label: B
options.text: Quaternary carbons appear as intense inverted negative peaks.

options.label: C
options.text: Quaternary carbons split into quartets.

options.label: D
options.text: Quaternary carbons (bearing zero hydrogens) produce NO signal in DEPT-135, appearing only in the broadband decoupled ¹³C spectrum in Chapter 12.

questions.correct_answer: Quaternary carbons (bearing zero hydrogens) produce NO signal in DEPT-135, appearing only in the broadband decoupled ¹³C spectrum in Chapter 12.
questions.explanation: DEPT relies on polarization transfer from directly attached protons; carbons without protons give zero signal in DEPT.

questions.topic: Ch12 Mass Spec M+2 Isotope Pattern
questions.question: What isotopic signature in mass spectrometry confirms the presence of a single bromine atom in a Chapter 12 compound?

options.label: A
options.text: Twin molecular ion peaks M⁺ and (M+2)⁺ of approximately equal intensity (1:1 ratio) separated by 2 m/z units in Chapter 12.

options.label: B
options.text: A 3:1 ratio of M⁺ to (M+2)⁺.

options.label: C
options.text: A 100:1 ratio.

options.label: D
options.text: A single peak with no isotopes.

questions.correct_answer: Twin molecular ion peaks M⁺ and (M+2)⁺ of approximately equal intensity (1:1 ratio) separated by 2 m/z units in Chapter 12.
questions.explanation: The ~1:1 natural abundance of 79Br and 81Br isotopes produces diagnostic twin peaks of equal height.

questions.topic: Ch12 Mass Spec Chlorine Isotope Pattern
questions.question: What isotopic signature confirms the presence of a single chlorine atom in a Chapter 12 mass spectrum?

options.label: B
options.text: A 1:1 ratio of M⁺ to (M+2)⁺.

options.label: C
options.text: Molecular ion peaks M⁺ and (M+2)⁺ in an approximately 3:1 intensity ratio separated by 2 m/z in Chapter 12.

options.label: D
options.text: A single M⁺ peak only.

questions.correct_answer: Molecular ion peaks M⁺ and (M+2)⁺ in an approximately 3:1 intensity ratio separated by 2 m/z in Chapter 12.

questions.question: What fragment ion is generated by α-cleavage of a Chapter 12 heteroatom-containing radical cation?

options.label: A
options.text: A neutral alkane molecule.

options.label: B
options.text: A high-energy dication.

options.label: C
options.text: A resonance-stabilized oxonium, iminium, or sulfonium cation with expulsion of the largest alkyl radical in Chapter 12.

options.label: D
options.text: A naked proton.

questions.correct_answer: A resonance-stabilized oxonium, iminium, or sulfonium cation with expulsion of the largest alkyl radical in Chapter 12.

questions.question: How does the spin-spin coupling constant (J, in Hz) between two coupled protons behave when magnetic field strength (MHz) is increased?

options.label: A
options.text: J-value increases linearly with spectrometer frequency.

options.label: B
options.text: J-value drops to zero at high fields.

options.label: C
options.text: The coupling constant J (Hz) remains strictly constant and invariant with field strength, whereas chemical shift separation (Hz) increases proportionally in Chapter 12.

options.label: D
options.text: J-value doubles every 100 MHz.

questions.correct_answer: The coupling constant J (Hz) remains strictly constant and invariant with field strength, whereas chemical shift separation (Hz) increases proportionally in Chapter 12.
questions.explanation: Scalar coupling J is an intrinsic molecular property mediated by bonding electrons, independent of external field B0.

questions.question: In a ¹H NMR spectrum of a Chapter 12 target, how are relative proton counts determined from integration curves?

options.label: A
options.text: By measuring the relative vertical step heights of the integration traces, which are directly proportional to the number of protons giving rise to each peak in Chapter 12.

options.label: B
options.text: By measuring the width of the peaks at half-height.

options.label: C
options.text: By counting the number of split sub-peaks.

options.label: D
options.text: By measuring the chemical shift in ppm.

questions.correct_answer: By measuring the relative vertical step heights of the integration traces, which are directly proportional to the number of protons giving rise to each peak in Chapter 12.
questions.explanation: Integration curve area is directly proportional to the relative number of resonant hydrogen nuclei.

questions.question: What systematic sequence is optimal for determining an unknown organic structure in Chapter 12 from spectral data?

options.label: A
options.text: Use only mass spectrometry without NMR.

options.label: B
options.text: Guess the structure from boiling point alone.

options.label: C
options.text: Assume all unknowns are symmetrical polymers.

options.label: D
options.text: Calculate HDI from MS formula → Identify functional groups via IR → Determine carbon framework via ¹³C/DEPT → Assemble connectivity and stereochemistry via ¹H NMR in Chapter 12.
